programs.haiku:
"""Finnish-text detector for layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5120.

This component fires on Finnish-language text: near 0 in English, German, Swedish or code,
roughly 1-2 on most tokens of Finnish prose, and up to ~5-7 on Finnish word endings and
inflected pieces. The program tracks how Finnish the current document looks so far: an
exponentially decayed share of its word tokens that are Finnish function words, carry
typical Finnish endings, or contain a/o-umlauts. It predicts a level that rises with that
share, scaled down on tokens that are not Finnish-looking. A new document resets it.
"""
READS = ()
FINNISH_WORDS = frozenset(
    "ja oli että sekä myös joka jotka kuin hän kanssa minä sinä hänen meidän kuten voi "
    "olla vuonna suomessa mutta ovat kuitenkin sitten vielä mukaan jälkeen tämä tämän "
    "tässä sitä siitä kaikki paljon hyvä ollut olivat tulee tänään koska vaan noin kautta "
    "lisäksi samoin jo nyt aina".split()
)
FINNISH_SUFFIXES = ("ssa", "ssä", "sta", "stä", "lla", "llä", "ksi", "ista", "iin", "aan", "ään", "ien", "ille", "inen", "iset", "ita", "itä")

def finnish_token(tok):
    if "ä" in tok or "ö" in tok:
        return True
    return tok.endswith(FINNISH_SUFFIXES)

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2] or carry is None:
        level = 0.0
    else:
        level = carry
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if not tok.isalpha():
        return level, 0.0
    is_fi = tok in FINNISH_WORDS or finnish_token(tok)
    level = 0.95 * level + 0.05 * (1.0 if is_fi else 0.0)
    value = 4.5 * level * (1.0 if is_fi else 0.3)
    return level, value

"""Give a tiny positive estimate for lowercase tokens without leading space.

This is only a weak cue for word-internal pieces, not a detector of individual bursts.
"""
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token and not token[0].isspace() and token[0].islower():
        return None, 0.003
    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""A token-level reply-versus-follow-up-question heuristic.

Named reply words (yes, no, well, actually, etc.) generally give positive
values. Question-opening words give negative values after a recent question.
The question cue fades with token distance, and capitalization and leading
spaces distinguish opening words from lowercase pieces. A recent Wait and
phrases such as But no provide additional correction cues.

Following commas/periods retain a reply or discourse-marker signal; A: and
Answer: are answer labels. Spaced ? ... : punctuation has a longer-lived
alternative/conditional cue. An initial question mark has a negative value.
A small translated lexicon covers some analogous discourse words. Other
tokens return zero; small token-specific background responses are omitted.
State resets at document boundaries. Nothing judges the truth of an answer.
"""

READS = ()

# Lowercase baseline, capitalized baseline, and their question increments.
REPLIES = {
    'yes': (1.39, 1.86, 3.42, 3.35),
    'no': (0.14, 0.73, 2.45, 3.20),
    'not': (-0.06, 0.29, 1.18, 2.45),
    'well': (0.11, 1.20, 1.97, 3.65),
    'wait': (0.23, 0.30, 0.44, 0.68),
    'actually': (0.79, 1.42, 0.71, 1.50),
    'indeed': (0.57, 0.85, 0.81, 0.60),
    'yeah': (1.00, 1.47, 0.38, 1.40),
    'yep': (0.80, 0.95, 0.40, 0.80),
    'sure': (0.02, 1.00, 0.65, 1.90),
    'certainly': (0.23, 1.30, 1.45, 1.30),
    'absolutely': (0.39, 2.60, 0.84, 0.60),
    'definitely': (0.33, 1.17, 0.84, 0.71),
    'probably': (0.15, 0.85, 1.29, 1.95),
    'maybe': (-0.04, 0.17, 1.03, 1.44),
    'hmm': (-0.06, 0.17, 0.00, 1.23),
    'ah': (0.03, 0.45, 0.18, 0.85),
    'oh': (0.04, 0.28, 0.15, 1.11),
    'okay': (0.24, 0.44, 0.39, 0.50),
    'right': (-0.09, 0.17, 0.41, 0.70),
    'only': (0.01, 0.25, 0.37, 1.10),
    'unfortunately': (0.38, 0.66, 0.00, 0.30),
}
WH_QUESTIONS = set('how what why who where which'.split())
AUX_QUESTIONS = set('can could is are do does did was were have has'.split())
MODAL_QUESTIONS = set('should would will'.split())
QUESTIONS = AUX_QUESTIONS | MODAL_QUESTIONS
ANSWER_STARTS = set('it that the this there you we let a'.split())
CONNECTIVES = {
    'furthermore': -0.54, 'additionally': -0.31, 'moreover': -0.29,
    'finally': -0.30, 'alternatively': -0.08, 'also': -0.10,
}
COMMAS = {
    'yes': (0.34, 0.77), 'no': (0.32, 0.46),
    'well': (0.07, 0.31), 'wait': (0.09, 0.13),
    'hmm': (0.08, 0.18), 'actually': (0.12, 0.32),
    'sure': (0.10, 0.44), 'yeah': (0.24, 0.44),
    'moreover': (-0.50, -0.70), 'also': (-0.20, -0.57),
    'furthermore': (-0.40, -0.55), 'finally': (-0.25, -0.52),
    'additionally': (-0.28, -0.42), 'alternatively': (-0.22, -0.22),
}

# Other-language discourse markers: Chinese/Japanese qualifications and
# Russian yes; question words in Chinese, Russian and Spanish.
OTHER_REPLIES = {
    '其实': (0.83, 1.54), '其實': (0.46, 0.05),  # actually/in fact
    '当然': (0.73, 0.12), '當然': (0.48, 0.90),  # of course
    '嗯': (0.73, 0.13), '确实': (0.32, 0.0),  # mm; indeed
    '実は': (0.63, 0.07), 'もちろん': (0.76, 0.0),  # in fact; of course
}
OTHER_QUESTIONS = {
    '如何': (0.16, -1.52), '为什么': (-0.15, -1.54),  # how; why
    'как': (0.03, -0.63), 'почему': (-0.13, 0.0),  # how; why
    'qué': (-0.23, -0.66),  # what
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        distance, since_wait = 10000, 10000
        previous, spaced_question = '', False
        first = True
    else:
        _, distance, since_wait, previous, spaced_question = carry
        first = False
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().strip('\"“”‘’')
    lower = word.lower()
    capital = int(bool(word) and word[0].isupper())
    spaced = token.startswith(' ')
    # Strength of a recent question cue, using only the past.
    q = distance ** -0.8 if distance <= 128 else 0.0
    opening_q = q if spaced else 0.8 * q
    value = 0.0
    if lower in REPLIES:
        base_lo, base_hi, boost_lo, boost_hi = REPLIES[lower]
        if capital:
            if lower == 'wait':
                opening_q = q if spaced else 0.45*q
            elif lower == 'hmm':
                opening_q = q if spaced else 0.60*q
            value = base_hi + boost_hi * opening_q
        else:
            value = base_lo + boost_lo*q
            if lower in ('no', 'not', 'actually') and since_wait <= 4:
                value += {'no': 0.82, 'not': 0.57,
                          'actually': 0.33}[lower] / since_wait
            if previous.lower() in (',', 'but'):
                value += {'no': 0.53, 'not': 0.25, 'well': 0.34}.get(lower, 0.0)
            # Bare lowercase pieces differ from space-prefixed reply words.
            if not spaced and lower in ('yes', 'no', 'well'):
                base, boost = {'yes': (0.64, 1.57), 'no': (0.35, 0.87),
                               'well': (0.29, 0.07)}[lower]
                value = base + boost*q
    elif lower in OTHER_REPLIES:
        base, boost = OTHER_REPLIES[lower]
        value = base + boost*q
    elif lower == 'да':  # Russian yes
        value = 0.62 + 1.41*q if capital else -0.02 + 0.41*q
    elif lower in OTHER_QUESTIONS:
        base, boost = OTHER_QUESTIONS[lower]
        if capital and lower in ('как', 'почему'):
            base, boost = (-0.16, -1.47) if lower == 'как' else (-0.23, -1.13)
        value = base + boost*q
    elif lower in ('-no', '/no'):  # The binary alternative yes-no / yes/no
        value = 1.50 if previous.lower() == 'yes' else 0.40
    elif lower in WH_QUESTIONS:
        strong = lower in ('how', 'what', 'why')
        value = (-0.10 - (2.20 if strong else 1.70)*opening_q
                 if capital else 0.04 - (1.10 if strong else 0.40)*q)
    elif lower in QUESTIONS:
        value = (-0.15 - (1.0 if lower in MODAL_QUESTIONS else 1.7)*opening_q
                 if capital else -0.20*q)
    elif lower in ANSWER_STARTS:
        value = 0.03 + 0.80*opening_q if capital else 0.12*q
    elif lower == 'because':
        value = 0.17 + 1.18*opening_q if capital else 0.92*q
    elif lower == 'answer':
        value = 0.39 + 1.03*opening_q if capital else 0.15 + 1.47*q
    elif lower in ('or', 'and'):
        value = -1.20*opening_q if capital else 0.01 - 0.35*q
    elif lower in CONNECTIVES:
        value = CONNECTIVES[lower] - 0.40*q
    elif word == ':':
        value = 0.20 + 1.30*q if spaced else -0.02 + 1.04*q
        if spaced and spaced_question and distance <= 128:
            value = 2.60 * distance ** -0.3
        if previous.lower() in ('a', 'answer'):
            value += 0.55 if '\n' not in token else 0.30
    elif word in (']:', '):', '：'):
        value = 0.70*q
    elif word == ',':
        if previous.lower() in COMMAS:
            base = COMMAS[previous.lower()][int(previous[:1].isupper())]
            value = base + 0.40*q
    elif word in ('.', '!') and previous.lower() in ('yes', 'no'):
        value = 0.15 + 0.55*q
    elif word == '?':
        value = 0.13 - 0.46*q if spaced else -0.03 - 0.53*q
        if first:
            value = -1.32 if '\n' in token else -2.26
    if ('?' in token or '？' in token) and '<' not in token:
        distance = 0
        spaced_question = token.startswith(' ?')
    if lower == 'wait':
        since_wait = 0
    return (doc, distance + 1, since_wait + 1, word, spaced_question), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Reply-opener axis of layer 0, MLP down_proj unit 5121.

What it does, in plain terms: this unit fires on the word that opens an answer. The
clearest case is "No", "Yes", "Not" or "Well" at the start of a sentence right after a
question ("...? No, ..."), which gives about 2.5. The same word at a sentence start with no
question before it gives about 0.7, and "no"/"well" mid-sentence give a weak value. "Yes",
"actually", "indeed", "absolutely" and similar words count anywhere, a little more after a
question. Softer reply words ("Wait", "Hmm", "Maybe", "Because", "Okay") count only at a
sentence start, weakly.

It goes negative on the words that open a new question ("Why", "What", "How", "Is", "Can")
at a sentence start right after a question (about -1), and on sentence connectives
("Furthermore", "Additionally", "Also"), about -0.45 after a question and -0.13 otherwise.
The comma right after such a word takes 40% of its value.

"After a question" means the most recent sentence-ending mark was "?", within 60 tokens.
Everything else is 0. The program is a hand-picked lexicon plus those rules; it keeps only the
last reply word's value and the last sentence-end position, so it runs in constant time per token.
"""

READS = ()

# Words that count anywhere in a sentence, and their value there.
ANYWHERE = {
    "yes": 1.5, "yeah": 1.2, "yep": 1.2, "actually": 0.9, "indeed": 0.6,
    "absolutely": 0.5, "definitely": 0.4, "certainly": 0.4, "probably": 0.3,
}
# Words that count only at the start of a sentence, and their value there.
SENTENCE_START = {
    "no": 1.0, "not": 1.0, "well": 1.2, "sure": 0.8, "right": 0.5, "because": 0.5,
    "maybe": 0.5, "unfortunately": 0.5, "hmm": 0.4, "wait": 0.4, "okay": 0.4,
    "oh": 0.4, "ah": 0.4, "perhaps": 0.3, "generally": 0.3,
}
# "no" and "well" keep a weak value mid-sentence.
MID_SENTENCE_NO_WELL = {"no", "well"}
QUESTION_WORDS = {
    "why", "what", "how", "which", "who", "where", "when", "is", "are", "was", "do", "does",
    "did", "can", "could", "should", "would", "will", "have", "has",
}
CONNECTIVES = {"furthermore", "moreover", "additionally", "finally", "also", "and", "or", "alternatively"}
SENTENCE_END = (".", "?", "!", "\n")
MAX_GAP = 60  # tokens since the question mark that still count as "after a question"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (position of the last "?", position of the last sentence end, value of the last opener)
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    last_q, last_end, opener = (-10**9, -10**9, 0.0) if new_doc or carry is None else carry
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if "?" in tok:
        last_q = t
    if any(c in tok for c in SENTENCE_END):
        last_end = t
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    prev = "" if new_doc else prefix.token_strings[-2]
    starts = new_doc or prev.strip() == "" or prev.endswith(SENTENCE_END)
    asked = last_q == last_end and t - last_q <= MAX_GAP
    value = 0.0
    if word in ANYWHERE:
        value = ANYWHERE[word] * (1.5 if asked else 1.0)
    elif word in SENTENCE_START and starts:
        value = SENTENCE_START[word] * (2.5 if asked else 0.7)
    elif word in MID_SENTENCE_NO_WELL:
        value = SENTENCE_START[word] * (0.8 if asked else 0.25)
    elif starts and asked and word in QUESTION_WORDS:
        value = -1.0
    elif starts and word in CONNECTIVES:
        value = -0.45 if asked else -0.13
    if value != 0.0 and (word in ANYWHERE or word in SENTENCE_START or starts):
        opener = value
    elif word == "," and prev.strip().lower() in ANYWHERE | SENTENCE_START.keys():
        value = 0.4 * opener
    return (last_q, last_end, opener), value
programs.luna:
"""Approximate conversational checks and answers at short lexical cues.

“Wait” and “Hmm” often start a reconsideration; “yes” and “no” mark an
answer or correction. Questions, answer wording, and paragraph starts make
these cues more informative. The rule is deliberately small and misses many
other reasons this component activates.
"""
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = "" if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = current.strip().lower()
    tail = previous[-70:].lower()
    opening = previous.rstrip(" \t").endswith("\n")
    question = "?" in tail[-45:]
    checking = any(cue in tail[-35:] for cue in ("wait", "hmm", "let me", "maybe"))
    cue = opening or question or checking

    value = 0.0
    if word == "wait":
        value = 0.70 if question else 0.45 if opening else 0.55 if checking else 0.30
    elif word == "no":
        implication = tail.rstrip().endswith(("⇒", "->", "→"))
        value = 0.90 if cue else 0.75 if implication else 0.55
    elif word == "yes":
        answer = "answer" in tail[-40:] or tail.rstrip().endswith("so")
        value = 1.50 if cue or answer else 0.90
    elif word == "yep":
        value = 0.90 if cue or tail.rstrip().endswith((".", "!", "→")) else 0.40
    elif word == "hmm":
        value = 0.65 if cue else 0.30
    elif word == "actually":
        value = 0.60
    elif word == "let":
        value = 0.50 if cue else 0.20
    elif word == "ah":
        value = 0.45 if cue else 0.20
    elif word in {"the", "a", "you"} and question:
        value = 0.60
    elif word == "well" and (opening or tail.rstrip().endswith(",")):
        value = 0.45
    elif word == ":" and (
        "answer" in tail[-40:]
        or "?" in tail[-20:]
        or opening
    ):
        value = 0.50
    elif word in {"當然", "当然"}:
        value = 0.45

    return (doc, (previous + current)[-100:]), value

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a modality-sensitive contrast between states and actions.

Knowledge, desire, necessity and state words have negative sensitivities;
helping, accomplishing and ease words have positive sensitivities. A preceding
infinitive or auxiliary strengthens them. Two-token memory also handles short
auxiliary/adverb chains and a few complement constructions, resetting between
documents. Unclassified English words get a weak grammar-only response;
other unmatched tokens are silent. Token-specific lexical variation is omitted.
"""
READS = ()

# (ordinary offset, signed sensitivity, words).
# Coefficients were fitted on training data and shared within each word class.
CLASSES = (
    # Knowing and understanding, including their participles.
    (-0.012, -1.780, 'know knowing knew'),
    (-0.035, -1.235, 'known'),
    (-0.034, -0.778, 'understand understood remember comprehend'),
    # Desire, necessity, feelings, appearances and judgments.
    (0.062, -2.033, 'need want wanted wanting wish prefer'),
    (0.088, -1.383, 'require required needed expect expected desired'),
    (-0.018, -0.844, 'feel felt feeling hope hoping believe love'),
    (0.011, -0.889, 'seem appear'),
    (0.046, -0.770, 'assume assumed guess appreciate appreciated sure obvious'
     ' content necessary possible available apparent ready worth'
     ' afraid important welcome entitled eligible interested'
     ' desirable likely critical'),
    # Static relations, permissions, and dependency.
    (0.054, -0.503, 'include contain involve consist refer mean avoid allow'
     ' allowed accept seek encourage support obtain meet fit suit'
     ' exist permit belong suppose'),
    (0.024, -0.644, 'depend depended'),
    # Statements and their passive/participial forms.
    (0.038, -0.424, 'say note suggest recommend describe define indicate think'
     ' predict explain estimate argue admit notice recognize agree'
     ' call'),
    (0.060, -0.658, 'said called noted suggested recommended described defined'
     ' indicated thought predicted deemed related associated'),
    # Helping, using things, and operations that produce results.
    (-0.022, 0.759, 'help lead cause reach reached'),
    (-0.062, 0.452, 'use used provide achieve access protect'),
    (-0.035, 0.495, 'done written edited achieved applied replaced solved placed'
     ' removed arranged accomplished added extended adjusted'
     ' converted reduced improved'),
    (-0.021, 0.231, 'make put do return improve read write solve continue learn'
     ' tell save reduce handle set happen arrange accomplish'
     ' replace eliminate spread'),
    # Habituality contrasts with ease, speed and successful execution.
    (0.008, -1.011, 'normally usually generally often currently typically'),
    (0.046, -0.395, 'probably always sometimes simply just already'),
    (0.010, 0.585, 'easily greatly significantly completely further quickly'
     ' effectively safely automatically soon eventually'),
    # Common Chinese counterparts of those semantic classes.
    (0.058, -0.514, '知道 了解 理解 明白 懂 见 見'),
    (-0.062, -1.186, '想 希望 觉得 覺得 相信 感到 不要'),
    (0.008, -1.061, '要 需要 要求'),
    (0.091, 0.688, '实现 實現 达到 達到 做到 解决 解決'),
    (0.072, 0.481, '帮助 幫助 提供 提高 改善'),
    (-0.039, 0.500, '使用 利用'),
    (0.014, -0.459, '说 說'),
)
RESPONSE = {word: (offset, strength)
            for offset, strength, words in CLASSES for word in words.split()}

# Strength of the preceding grammatical cue; ordinary context is weak.
CUES = (
    (.50, 'to'),
    (1., 'can cannot'),
    (.65, "will shall 'll ’ll"),
    (.35, "would 'd ’d"),
    (.60, 'could'),
    (.40, 'may'),
    (.30, 'might'),
    (.55, 'should must'),
    (.63, 'be'),
    (.46, 'been'),
    (.55, "have has had 've ’ve"),
    (.09, "is are am 's ’s"),
    (.17, 'was were'),
    (.19, "not never no 't ’t"),
    (.07, 'i'),
    (.04, 'you we they he she it'),
    (.03, 'the a an'),
    (.30, 'still'),
    (.20, 'even really'),
    (.70, 'gotta wanna gonna'),
    (.75, 'please'),
    (1., '能 能够 能夠 可以 不能 无法 無法'),
    (.60, '会 會 将 將 要 需要 必须 必須 应该 應該'),
    (.40, '不 没 沒 未'),
    (.65, '在 曾 刚刚 剛剛'),
)
CUE = {word: value for value, words in CUES for word in words.split()}
ADVERBS = set(('also only just not never always often usually normally '
               'generally currently probably possibly really already still '
               'simply easily quickly completely fully certainly definitely '
               'well typically').split())
MODALS = set('can cannot will would could should must may might shall'.split())
DESIRE = set('need want wanted wanting'.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, before_previous, last_value = '', '', 0.
    else:
        _, previous, before_previous, last_value = carry
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().lower()
    cue = CUE.get(previous, .075) if previous else .18
    # Let an auxiliary govern across one intervening adverb.
    if previous in ADVERBS and CUE.get(before_previous, 0.) >= .30:
        cue = .25 * cue + .75 * CUE[before_previous]
    if word in ('hoping', 'wanting', 'feeling') and previous in (
            'am', 'is', 'are', "'m", '’m', "'re", '’re'):
        cue = .35
    if previous in ('be', 'been') and before_previous in CUE:
        cue *= .6 + .8 * CUE[before_previous]
    if word == 'know' and previous in ('me', 'us', 'him', 'her', 'them', 'you'):
        if before_previous == 'let':
            cue = .35
    # The central rule: word-class bias plus grammar-scaled sensitivity.
    if word in RESPONSE:
        offset, strength = RESPONSE[word]
        if word in ('help', 'lead', 'cause', 'reach') and previous == 'to':
            cue = .25
        value = offset + strength * cue
    # Auxiliary uses, modal scaffolding, and complement phrases.
    elif word == 'have':
        value = {'to': -.24, 'can': -.45, 'cannot': -.45, 'will': -.31,
                 'would': -.14, 'could': -.22, 'should': -.23,
                 'must': -.28, 'i': .07}.get(previous, .02)
    elif word == 'be':
        value = {'to': .08, 'should': .16, 'would': -.08,
                 'might': -.08, 'may': -.04}.get(previous, 0.)
    elif word in ('also', 'only') and previous in MODALS | {'to'}:
        value = .20
    elif word == 'also' and previous in ('is', 'are', 'am'):
        value = -.06
    elif word in ('then', 'either', 'thus', 'otherwise') and previous in MODALS:
        value = .35
    elif (word in ('i', 'you', 'we', 'they', 'he', 'she', 'it')
          and previous in MODALS):
        value = .25 if previous in ('can', 'cannot', 'could') else .15
    elif word == 'not' and previous in MODALS | {'to', 'be'}:
        value = -.30 * cue if previous not in ('may', 'might') else 0.
    elif word == 'about' and previous in ('to', 'be', 'can'):
        value = -.38
    elif word == 'to' and previous in DESIRE:
        value = .30 * last_value
    elif word == 'of' and previous == 'need':
        value = -.38
    elif (word == '的'
          and previous.endswith(('值得', '应该', '應該', '必须', '必須'))):
        value = -.45
    elif not previous and raw.startswith(' ') and word in MODALS:
        if word in ('would', 'might'):
            value = -.16
        elif word == 'may':
            value = -.29
        elif word == 'should':
            value = -.94
        elif word in ('can', 'must'):
            value = -.76
        else:
            value = -.56
        if raw.strip()[0].isupper():
            value *= .6
    elif not previous and word in ('可以', '应该', '應該'):
        value = -1.
    elif word.isascii() and word.isalpha():
        value = {'can': .10, 'cannot': .10, 'could': .05, 'may': .05,

starts in the middle of a German sentence, i.e. a noun opening right after an
article, preposition, conjunction or adjective ("den Gr-uppen", "die Be-ziehungen",
"und Zeit", "einen An-..."). It is strongest on the first piece of a noun, and
weak when the capital follows a full stop (sentence start) or a capitalised
English name appears. Lowercase German words (der, und, ist, durch) give a small
negative value. Everything else is zero.

The program only reads tokens up to the current one. It decides "German" from
German function words earlier in the same document.

READS = ()

GERMAN_FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    "der die das und ist nicht sich ein eine einen einem zu mit auf für von dem "
    "den des auch werden wird sind es im als bei nach wie aber oder dass daß sie "
    "er wir ihr ihre sein seine hat haben wurde wurden noch nur so zwischen".split()
)
SENTENCE_END = frozenset([".", "!", "?", ":", ";", "\n", ""])
WINDOW = 30  # recent tokens used to decide "German"
NOUN_START = 1.4  # capitalised German word mid-sentence
SENTENCE_START = 0.0  # capitalised German word after a full stop
LOWERCASE_GERMAN = -0.23  # lowercase German function word or verb


def german_context(prefix):
    """True if at least two German function words occur in the recent same-document text."""
    t = prefix.position
    hits = 0
    for i in range(max(0, t - WINDOW), t + 1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != prefix.document_ids[t]:
            continue
        if prefix.token_strings[i].strip().lower() in GERMAN_FUNCTION_WORDS:
            hits += 1
    return hits >= 2

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    if not word.isalpha() or not token.startswith(" "):
        return None, 0.0
    if not german_context(prefix):
        return None, 0.0
    if word[0].isupper():
        before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if prefix.position > 0 else ""
        value = SENTENCE_START if before in SENTENCE_END else NOUN_START
    else:
        value = LOWERCASE_GERMAN
    return None, float(value)

"""Layer-0 MLP neuron 5132 (down_proj): a "contrast / concession / consequence connective" detector.

It goes strongly negative on the word that opens a clause which contrasts with, concedes
against, or follows from the one before: English "but", "however", "rather", "whereas",
"because", "although", "while"; Chinese 而 (and its compounds 然而, 从而, 而且, 而是),

nhưng, jedoch, しかし). Ordinary words, including "and", "so", "if", "since", score 0.

Values are the mean activation for each word, so the program is a lookup of how strongly
each connective fires. A bare 而 is the strongest (about -9), so it dominates the variance.
"""

    "but": -1.4, "rather": -1.35, "whereas": -2.0, "because": -1.0, "however": -1.0,
    "although": -0.9, "though": -0.75, "while": -0.7, "instead": -0.65, "thus": -0.43,

    "jedoch": -0.65, "しかし": -1.2, "そして": -1.5, "于是": -1.3, "然后": -1.6, "然後": -1.6,

"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5133 (layer 0, MLP down projection), as a rule.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It responds to backslash-escaped double quotes: the token made of a backslash followed by
  a double quote. These appear when code or a quoted string is nested inside another string,
  for example a shell command or Python snippet inside a JSON tool call. A bare escaped quote,
  or one preceded by a space, "(" or "=", gives about +1.9. An escaped quote fused with the
  punctuation after it (a comma, colon, parenthesis or ">") gives about +1.0.
- An escaped single quote (backslash followed by an apostrophe) gives about +0.9.
- It is negative (about -0.7) on a newline that follows a chat-template marker: "assistant",
  "user", "<|im_end|>", "<think>", "</think>", "<tool_call>" or "<tool_response>". These are
  the newlines that open a new turn or tool block.
- Everywhere else it predicts 0. It is stateless: it looks at the newest token and the one
  before it, within the same document.

The rule explains about 60% of the variance on the training sample checked. Token identity
alone would explain about 70%; the rest is diffuse context dependence that is not captured.
"""

READS = ()

BACKSLASH_QUOTE = "\\" + '"'     # the two-character token: backslash, double quote
BACKSLASH_APOS = "\\" + "'"      # backslash, single quote
CHAT_MARKERS = {
    "assistant", "user", "<|im_end|>", "<think>", "</think>", "<tool_call>", "<tool_response>",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    if BACKSLASH_QUOTE in token:
        value = 1.9 if token.endswith(BACKSLASH_QUOTE) else 1.0
    elif BACKSLASH_APOS in token:
        value = 0.9
    elif token in ("\n", "\n\n") and previous in CHAT_MARKERS:
        value = -0.7
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Mark tokens naming trouble, harm, illness, or defects with a negative score.

The component is most visible on concrete bad conditions and on words such as
problem, error, damage, and disease.  This short lexical rule captures that
direction, but it cannot recover the component's context-sensitive strength.
"""

import re

READS = ()

_STRONG = (
    "problem", "problems", "enfermedad", "enfermed", "disease",
    "illness", "disaster", "災", "灾", "鬼城",
)

_TROUBLE = (
    "issue", "error", "fault", "failure", "wrong", "bad", "broken",
    "defective", "damage", "deterioration", "trouble", "mistake",
    "danger", "enemy", "toxic", "trash", "virus", "infection",
    "symptom", "acne", "cancer", "injury", "death", "depression",
    "inflammation", "poverty", "incarceration", "felony", "misdemeanor",
    "offense", "accident", "腐", "朽", "鬼", "卫生",
)

_WORDS = re.compile(
    r"(?<!\w)(?:" + "|".join(
        re.escape(word) for word in _STRONG + _TROUBLE
    ) + r")(?!\w)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        previous = ""

        previous = carry[1]

    text = previous + token
    new_start = len(previous)
    value = 0.0
    for match in _WORDS.finditer(text):
        if match.end() <= new_start:
            continue
        word = match.group().casefold()
        value = -1.25 if word in _STRONG else -0.75

    return (document, text[-80:]), value

"""Layer-0 MLP unit 5136: an "in"-preposition detector for Romance-language text.

The unit dips negative on the preposition "in" written as "en" or "em" (Spanish and
Portuguese), and on the same word in other languages: na, nas (Portuguese, Polish),
dans, nel, nella, nelle (French, Italian), au (French), pela (Portuguese), and on other
Spanish and Portuguese prepositions (sur, por, im, al, para, con, no). It stays near zero
on English "in", "of", "to", and on "en" used as an article in Danish or Dutch.

How deep the dip goes depends on the language of the text so far. For the Spanish and
Portuguese words, the program counts what share of the words so far in the same document
are common Spanish or Portuguese function words, and scales the dip by it (at least a
fifth of full strength, full strength at 20% or more). So "en" in a Spanish sentence gives
a deep dip, and "en" in Danish or Dutch gives a shallow one. The French and Italian words
(dans, nel, nella, nelle, au) always get their full dip, because the word itself marks the
language.

The predicted value is negative and roughly in the component's own units.
"""

READS = ()

# Depth of the dip for each word in fully Spanish/Portuguese context.
GATED_DIP = {
    "en": 2.8, "em": 2.6, "na": 2.0, "nas": 1.8, "sur": 0.8, "por": 0.6, "im": 0.5,
    "al": 0.4, "no": 0.3, "para": 0.3, "con": 0.2,
}
# Words that are in-prepositions in their own language, so always at full depth.
FIXED_DIP = {"dans": 1.0, "nel": 1.8, "nella": 1.8, "nelle": 1.8, "au": 0.9, "pela": 1.6}
# Common Spanish and Portuguese function words, used to judge the language of the text.
SPANISH_PORTUGUESE = set(
    "el los las que y con para una es del al pero como más también sus le ya este "
    "esta entre cuando muy sin sobre hasta donde desde todo todos era fue son está "
    "están hay porque nos se lo das dos não uma uns mas você ele ela muito já isso "
    "ao seu sua seus suas eu foi são pelo pela dos no".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, 0)  # a new document: forget the language so far
    _, words, hits = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0
    spaced = token.startswith(" ") or token in ("En", "Em")
    if word in GATED_DIP and spaced:
        strength = min(1.0, 0.2 + 5.0 * hits / max(words, 1))
        value = -GATED_DIP[word] * strength
    elif word in FIXED_DIP and spaced:
        value = -FIXED_DIP[word]
    if token.startswith(" ") and word.isalpha():
        words += 1
        hits += word in SPANISH_PORTUGUESE
    return (doc, words, hits), value

BYTE_VALUES = list(range(33, 127)) + list(range(161, 173)) + list(range(174, 256))

SOME = {'有些', '有一些', '有一点'}
QUANTITY = {
    '有一', '有一个', '有一天', '有一位', '有一次', '有一种',
    '有两个', '有两种', '有几个', '有个', '有点', '有點',
    '有很多', '有许多', '有不少', '有多', '有哪些', '有些人',
}
EXISTENCE = {
    '有人', '有什么', '有何', '有多少', '有多大', '有多么',
    '有任何', '有钱', '有所', '也有',
}

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == '<|endoftext|>':
        value = 1.72
    elif token in SOME:
        value = 2.28
    elif token in QUANTITY:
        value = 1.43
    elif token in EXISTENCE:
        value = 0.62
    elif token in {'有', '还有', '還有', '都有', '有没有', '有的', '有着'}:
        value = 0.28

def fragment_value(prefix):
    """Distinguish an unfinished UTF-8 character from its completing byte."""
    token_id = int(prefix.token_ids[-1])
    if not 0 <= token_id < 256:
        return 0.0
    byte = BYTE_VALUES[token_id]
    if not 0x80 <= byte < 0xc0:
        return 0.0
    char = prefix.text_prefixes[-1][-1:]
    if char == '\ufffd':
        # A continuation byte that has not yet finished a character.
        previous = -1
        if (len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and
                prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]):

            if 0 <= previous_id < 256:

            return -1.7
        if 0xe4 <= previous <= 0xe9:  # CJK characters
            return -0.1
        if previous == 0xef:  # Includes font icons and presentation forms
            return -0.15
        return -0.35
    if not char:
        return 0.0
    category = unicodedata.category(char)
    if category == 'Co':
        return -0.7 if ord(char) < 0xf000 else -0.14
    if category == 'Cf':
        return -0.43
    if category in {'Mn', 'So'}:
        return -0.19
    if 0x3400 <= ord(char) <= 0x9fff:
        return 0.0
    return -0.05

    a dot (`.)`), a percent or plus sign (`%)`, `++)`), or another closing bracket

    (re.compile(QUOTE + r'[.;,]*\s*\n'), -0.5),   # string ends a line
    (re.compile(QUOTE + r';'), -0.45),            # string ends a statement
    (re.compile(QUOTE + r','), -0.2),             # string followed by a comma
    (re.compile(QUOTE + CLOSE), 0.44),            # closing quote, then a closing bracket
    (re.compile(r'\.' + CLOSE), 0.5),             # dot, then a closing bracket
    (re.compile(r'[%+*]' + CLOSE), 0.9),          # %) ++) *)
    (re.compile(CLOSE + CLOSE), 0.25),            # two closing brackets
    (re.compile(CLOSE + r'[.,]'), 0.07),          # closing bracket then dot or comma

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    for pattern, value in RULES:

    "time posts joined".split()

    "port node test tests run".split()

  other lowercase word piece                    -> 1
  capitalised word                              -> 0.2
  digits, punctuation, spaces                   -> 0

    "jego", "ich", "być", "już", "też", "które", "który", "która", "są", "był", "była",

            or lower in POLISH_WORDS

    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]

    for word in words.split()

    ('something someone another', 3.0),                 # indefinite selection
    ('oldest youngest largest smallest biggest', 2.5),   # superlatives

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

        value = LEXICON.get(previous, (0.0, 0.10))[1]

        value = DE_HEADS.get(previous, (0.0, 0.0))[1]

        value = LEXICON[word][0]

            value = DE_HEADS.get(word, (0.0, 0.0))[0]

"""Quantity-"of" detector (layer 0, MLP down_proj, unit 5182).

The unit responds to the word " of" in quantity and partitive phrases: "a number of",
"a lot of", "a couple of", "an amount of", "a kind of", "a variety of", "a portion of",
"part of", "a type of", "a percentage of". It is strongest after nouns of amount and kind,
weaker after nouns of part, type or measure, weaker still after relational nouns
("form of", "range of", "end of", "result of", "level of", "use of"), and near zero for
"of" after numbers, pronouns and names ("one of", "all of", "instance of", "place of").
The quantity words that themselves demand an "of" ("lot", "kind", "variety", "thousands",
"instead", "consists") are negative (-2) on their own token.
"""

READS = ()

# Amount and kind nouns: "a number of", "a lot of", "a kind of".
AMOUNT = {" number", " amount", " couple", " portion", " lot", " lots", " variety", " kind",
          " kinds", " sort", " Number"}
# Part, type and measure nouns: "part of", "type of", "thousands of", "percentage of".
PART = {" part", " parts", " type", " types", " plurality", " majority", " thousands",
        " hundreds", " millions", " dozens", " bunch", " piece", " fraction", "%", " percent",
        " Percent", " percentage", " volume", " bulk", " mix", " mixture", " proportion",
        " magnitude", " quantity", " amounts", " half", " pair", " series", " cent", " lack",
        " presence", " components", " nature", " purpose", " aspect"}
# Relational nouns and words that often take "of": "form of", "end of", "instead of".
RELATIONAL = {" form", " range", " quality", " level", " result", " end", " out", " instead",
              " combination", " ratio", " most", " many", " member", " set", " rest",
              " consists", " consist", " consisting", " consisted", " regardless", " composed",
              " side", " version", " use", " union", " terms", " sense", " loss", " ability",
              " snippet", " Department", " University", " Republic", " source", " cause"}
# Quantity words that themselves demand a following "of".
DEMANDS_OF = {" lot", " lots", " kind", " kinds", " variety", " thousands", " hundreds",
              " millions", " plurality", " majority", " instead", " consists", " consist",
              " regardless", " composed", " Instead", " instead"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    cur = tokens[-1]
    if cur == " of" and len(tokens) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev = tokens[-2]
        if prev in AMOUNT:
            return None, 3.0
        if prev in PART:
            return None, 2.0
        if prev in RELATIONAL:
            return None, 1.0
        return None, 0.0
    if cur in DEMANDS_OF:
        return None, -2.0
    return None, 0.0
